hyps.why: Beyond ~0.08 further increases push Adam into divergence/erratic training, so the step hurts much more there.
With lr 1e-5 to 1.3e-4 the model is undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing lr gives large gains.
Reducing an overly large lr restores stable training, giving big improvements only in the high band.
Tiny batches already give many noisy updates, so a larger lr adds instability rather than speed.
Larger batches cut the number of updates, worsening undertraining when the lr is tiny.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training under aggressive learning rates.
Smaller batches give more updates per epoch, compensating for a tiny step size.
Moving alpha from 0.13 toward 1 causes heavy weight shrinkage and underfitting, while increases at tiny alpha are negligible.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited so extra units help, whereas wide networks are saturated.
Deeper ReLU nets are more prone to instability and dead units under large learning rates.
